correctness.rationale: The core is the set of pairwise-incomparable ordered triples of the two-level finite crown. Every non-core point lies uniquely in one of four incidence classes L1,U1,L2,U2. Stepwise deletion removes L1 down beats and U1 up beats, followed by L2 up beats (their one-coordinate successors were U1) and U2 down beats (their one-coordinate predecessors were L1). Each class is an antichain and the unique opposite-rank witness survives. The residue has no beat points: for all-one-level configurations n>=4 has at least two admissible mixed successors from boundary edges of a three-element subset of an n-cycle, while n=3 has two distinct all-opposite-level successors arising from the two cyclic perfect matchings; mixed incomparable triples have at least two incomparable witnesses in both directions. This proves an exact finite-space strong deformation retract and uniqueness of the Stong core for every n>=3. The class-count identity gives size 2n(2n-4)(2n-5) and 12n(2n-3) deletions. For n=2, all 24 triples form two 12-point crowns with no beat points by complete finite enumeration. Standalone verify_core.py was executed successfully for n=2..12; those samples corroborate but do not replace the universal proof. Source: Barmak–Minian arXiv:math/0611156v1, Definition 2.3 (beat points, Stong core), and Minian arXiv:2205.11062v1.

originality.rationale: Same-object published research concerns two-point configurations of finite crowns and proves only their weak circle type, not the exact Stong core of three-point configurations. General Stong theory supplies an abstract existence/uniqueness statement; Minian’s relative poset Morse theory supplies reduction methods, not this four-class reduction or exact core size. General product cores do not give cores of deleted powers. The complete result for ordered triple configurations appears uncovered by targeted published-finding corpus, public literature, and same-object full-text comparison. Residual possibility of an unindexed equivalent statement is acknowledged, so the literature search is evidence of noncoverage, not a proof of global novelty.
residual_risks: Unindexed or unpublished three-particle finite-crown core theorem could exist; indexed absence does not establish uniqueness.
A general theorem on deleted Cartesian powers of height-two posets, if identified later, might subsume the four-stage reduction.
The geometric-simplicial configuration paper was compared at abstract/object level; its full text was not needed for a decisive claim but was not fully inspected.

value.rationale: The question is a natural next topological invariant after the known two-particle weak-equivalence theorem: the exact ordinary finite-space homotopy class, which is finer than weak homotopy and is characterized canonically by the Stong core. The result gives a complete infinite-family classification for three labeled configurations, exact core order and sharp n=2 boundary, with a direct four-stage structural reduction. This is neither a restatement of the known F2 case nor an arbitrary finite slice or textbook substitution. It provides the minimal finite model from which exact three-point homotopy questions can start. No general homology or geometric-circle equivalence is claimed.
